title: Foo Fighters Play First-Ever Hollywood Bowl Show With LA Philharmonic
summary: It marked the band's first time playing the venue in its more than three decades together.
contentText:
Foo Fighters paused their Take Cover Tour for a one-off performance with the Los Angeles Philharmonic at the Hollywood Bowl on Saturday (Aug. 22), joining conductor Gustavo Dudamel and the Youth Orchestra Los Angeles for a 15-song set honoring Dudamel’s final season with the Phil.

It marked the band’s first time playing the venue in its more than three decades together. Backed by full orchestra and choir, the band moved through a set blending hits with several deep cuts rarely aired live.

The night opened with “Times Like These” before running through “All My Life,” “The Pretender,” “Walk,” “My Hero,” “Learn to Fly,” “The Sky Is a Neighborhood” and “Run.” The rarities came in a cluster: “I Should Have Known,” from 2011’s Wasting Light , got its first performance since 2012; “Razor,” from 2005’s In Your Honor , returned for the first time since 2006; and “Home,” from 2007’s Echoes, Silence, Patience & Grace , got its first live outing since 2007.

The band also revived “A320,” a deep cut from the 1998 Godzilla soundtrack that originally featured string arrangements, making it a natural fit for the orchestral setting. Frontman Dave Grohl dedicated “Aurora” to late drummer Taylor Hawkins before the band closed the night with “Best of You,” “Home” and, finally, “Everlong.”

The concert was part of “Celebrating Gustavo at the Bowl,” a four-night tribute marking Dudamel’s 17th and final season as the LA Philharmonic’s music and artistic director. Dudamel will take over as music director of the New York Philharmonic beginning with its 2026-27 season.

Frontman Dave Grohl had previously performed with Dudamel and the orchestra at Coachella 2025, joining for orchestral versions of “The Sky Is a Neighborhood” and “Everlong.”

The Hollywood Bowl date came in the middle of a busy stretch for Foo Fighters, who played Rock in Rio in Brazil and filled in for the Pretty Reckless on a one-off support slot for AC/DC in St. Louis before the Dudamel show. The band’s own Take Cover Tour, a stadium run marking Foo Fighters’ fourth decade together, resumes in mid-September with dates across North America.
